## Disagreements

- **CAP-16** (L1 tip, L2 safe): A slow leak at 16 degrees with a 0.16 m CoM offset (above the 0.12 m limit, DQ-011) and load holding working. Level 1 loses balance as its centre-of-pressure limit (L cos(slope) x capacity, A3) shrinks and tips after the hold engages. Level 2 has CL-05's reverse-jointed legs standing on a knee bent 0.3 rad (DQ-027); it locks at 3.4 s and holds with the ankle at 20 kN m or more, tips at 15 kN m, and drops the cockpit with the knee at 15 kN m: the actuator-capacity boundary lies below the adopted torques (ankle 40.5, knee 26.5 kN m; sim/results/sizing-cf4.md).
- **SF-01/EC-07** (L1 tip, L2 hard-drop): Load holding fails during a slow leak at 18 degrees, so the walker is lost either way; the models differ in which actuator gives out first. Level 1 ties leg force and centre-of-pressure authority to the same capacity (A3, A4) and tips. Level 2 has CL-05's reverse-jointed legs standing on a knee bent 0.3 rad (DQ-027); its ankles keep the CoM over the foot while the legs sag, so it drops the cockpit at 3.1 m/s (HAZ-PIL-002) with the adopted torques and at any knee from 15 to 40 kN m, and tips with the ankle at 20 kN m or less.
- **SF-01/EC-08** (L1 tip, L2 safe): A slow leak at 19.5 degrees with load holding working; both levels lock at about 2.9 s. Before the lock, level 1's centre-of-pressure limit (A3) and leg sag (A4) let its CoM drift to the foot edge, so the locked body tips (A5) at 3.4 s. Level 2 has CL-05's reverse-jointed legs standing on a knee bent 0.3 rad (DQ-027); it keeps its CoM over the foot until the lock and holds with the ankle at any torque from 15 kN m up, and tips only with the knee at 15 kN m: here level 1's assumptions, not the actuators, decide.

Notes are AI drafts (I0). A disagreement is a finding about the models: the level that is closer to the real machine is unknown until hardware data exists.
